scope: Proposition 6.1 (Modulated delayed Haar estimate) of the manuscript “Almost-everywhere Fourier convergence in L log L” (preprints/Almost-everywhere-Fourier-convergence-in-L-log-L-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 075 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9a77d41e5b9b9beb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants C and d0 with the following property. Let d ≥ d0, put h = log log d, and let I ⊂ R be a half-open interval with 1/2 ≤ |I| ≤ 1. Let ρ : I → [0, ∞) be measurable, with ρ ≤ ed almost everywhere and mtop = 1 |I| ∫︂ I ρ ≤ 2. Give I its normalized uniform probability U. Write Fj for its depth-j dyadic sigma field, pj(x) for the depth-j interval containing x, and rj+1 for the sign that is +1 on the left child and −1 on the right child of each such interval. Let J ≥ 1 and Q ≥ 0 be integers. For 0 ≤ j < J, let ϵj : I → C be Fj+1-measurable with |ϵj| ≤ 1, and use the same ϵj for all modulations. The bits through depth J + 1 are retained, so the last output sign is rJ+1. Set τ(x) = min (︁ {0 ≤ j < J : Epj(x)ρ > e4h } ∪ {J} )︁ , Epv = 1 |p| ∫︂ p v(y) dy, and, with χu(y) = e2πiuy, define Hu I,J ρ(x) = ∑︂ 0≤j<τ(x) Epj(x)[ρ(Y )χu(Y )rj+1(Y )] ϵj(x)rj+2(x). Then ∫︂ I max u∈Z |u|≤Q |Hu I,J ρ(x)| dx |I| ≤ Cd. (6.1) The constants are independent of I, ρ, J, Q, and the multipliers. Consequently the same estimate holds with supu∈Z in place of the finite maximum.
